stories.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued through November, with two tankers attacked on 16 November. US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf on Tuesday.
stories.why_it_matters: Military escalation and hull strikes raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude and product ton-miles.
stories.latest: US military strike on an Iranian missile site at Qeshm Island reported Tuesday; separately, Week 46 freight weakness has spread to Gulf VLCC routes with East of Suez ballasters rising from 415 to 434.
sources: U.S. Military Strikes Iranian Missile Site Near Strait of Hormuz
Gulf Earnings Give Way as VLCC Ballasters Build East of Suez

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
stories.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea continue. Two merchant vessels have sunk off Bulgaria after reported drone attacks, with several seafarers injured and 31 crew rescued, following a wheat carrier capsizing earlier in the week.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region.
stories.latest: Two more merchant vessels sunk off Bulgaria, seafarers injured, 31 crew rescued.
sources: Seafarers injured as two vessels struck in Black Sea off Bulgaria

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations.
stories.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties, documents and vessel positions, and can strand tonnage outside compliant trade.
sources: How to Reduce False Positives in Vessel Screening Without Missing Real Risk

stories.title: US Jones Act waiver extended again
stories.what: A waiver allowing commodities to move between US ports on foreign-flagged ships has been extended for another 90 days, with the pause now past 230 days.
stories.why_it_matters: It keeps foreign-flag tonnage eligible for US coastwise cargoes, affecting US-flag demand and product tanker employment in domestic trades.
sources: Gulf Earnings Give Way as VLCC Ballasters Build East of Suez

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia arrangement on extra diesel for the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a ban on most diesel exports to end-January.
stories.why_it_matters: Export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment.
sources: Vietnam eyes more Russian LNG supplies

stories.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
stories.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue.
stories.why_it_matters: If reinstated, the fees would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
sources: Vestas CEO Calls For EU Crackdown on Chinese Software Used in Wind Sector
